# Query Carefully: Detecting the Unanswerables in Text-to-SQL Tasks

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#query-carefully)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.21345v1) · arXiv:2512.21345v1, 19 December 2025

**Reading coverage:** All 13 PDF pages: sections 1–6, references, pipeline figure and rendered result/UI figures 2–5; no appendix in this version.

**Additional inspected sources:** [Official implementation and data](https://github.com/JasminSaxer/QueryCarefully)

## Research question

Detect unsupported or ambiguous biomedical requests before plausible SQL is mistaken for a supported answer.

## Method

Llama 3.3 70B receives a reformatted OncoMX schema, no-answer rules and retrieved positive/negative demonstrations. A fallback requests SQL or refusal; an optional loop repairs execution errors up to three times.

## Evaluation

The study uses 99 answerable OncoMX development questions and 80 author-reviewed GPT-4o no-answer questions across eight categories. Negative demonstrations come from the same 80-question pool with the current question excluded; this is not a separately held-out negative retrieval corpus.

## What the results support

Balanced demonstrations improve no-answer detection. Execution-error repair removes database errors but can increase incorrect results. Missing values and column ambiguity remain difficult; the interface displays SQL, results and abstention explanations.

## Limits and qualifications

One model and biomedical database, ten negatives per category, reference-result evaluation and a shared negative-demonstration pool limit transfer.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A concrete refusal-prompting baseline, with useful evidence that executable SQL and successful error repair need not mean correct answers.
